trades.headline: Turn a season-ending Dart and banged-up McConkey into a healthy, ascending RB1 in Omarion Hampton
trades.summary: Dart needs season-ending knee surgery and won't help until 2027, and we're deep enough at WR to move McConkey; Hampton is fully healthy and stepping into a lead role for a rebuilding Njgriffin squad.

give: Dart suffered MCL/PCL/meniscus damage in Week 2, needs season-ending surgery, and isn't expected back until 2027.
McConkey is nursing a Week 1 rib injury; we're deep at WR (Nacua, Odunze, Lemon, M. Wilson) and can absorb the loss.
get: Hampton says his rookie-year ankle injuries are behind him and is set for a bigger workload in year two (FantasyCalc rank 8).
Mayfield fought through a Week 3 illness but had a full practice Friday and is not on the injury report.
you: Fills our thinnest position (RB) with a clear breakout-caliber back, replacing IR'd Jonah Coleman in the lineup.
Adds Superflex QB depth behind Hurts/Maye without touching either current starter.
them: 0-2 Njgriffin is thin at QB/TE and deep at RB/WR, so moving a surplus RB for a high-capital rookie QB fits a rebuild.
They bank Dart's long-term upside (ACL intact) for 2027 while adding a WR (McConkey) to their deep receiver room.

risks: Giants HC left open a slim chance Dart returns in the 2026 postseason, which would make this look like an early sell.
Hampton is still building back to a full workload post-injury, so touches could stay inconsistent for a few more weeks.

trades.headline: Sell a turnover-prone Maye for a bell-cow in Achane plus the Rams' new TE1 Ferguson
trades.summary: Maye has been erratic through two games and we're deep at QB, while Achane anchors Miami's backfield and Ferguson just took over as Sean McVay's clear TE1 — a real plus under your te_premium scoring.

give: Maye threw 3 INTs and lost a fumble in Week 1; we already start Hurts and roster Brissett/Young/Milroe behind him.
QB is our deepest position, so moving a Superflex QB2 doesn't touch our starting lineup at all.
get: Achane is Miami's clear lead back; he took a full practice Friday despite a questionable hip tag and profiles as an all-but-certain starter.
Ferguson logged 58% snaps, a 31% target share and 6 catches on 9 targets in Week 2, taking over the Rams' TE1 job — extra value with te_premium.
you: Directly fills both roster-thin spots (RB and TE) in a single trade, replacing IR'd Coleman and pairing Ferguson with Warren.
Leaves Hurts in place as our Superflex starter, so the current lineup doesn't get worse anywhere.
them: 2-0 CREAM TEAM is deep at QB/RB and thin at WR/TE, moving a buried TE (Ferguson) for a true Superflex starter in Maye.
Their own lineup math shows a gain from swapping Dak Prescott to Maye in Superflex (+1.2% team value).

risks: Maye limited his Week 2 turnovers (win over Pittsburgh) and could still hit his ceiling, making this a sell-low if he stabilizes.
Achane's hip is a game-time watch; a setback this week would blunt the immediate return on this deal.
